improv_extras.concept: advect particle dye through a stable-fluids (Navier-Stokes) velocity field with vortices — smoke/ink that curls and dissipates with real fluid feel

v1.feedback: The technique is solid — GPGPU point-vortex advection with spring homing keeps 100k particles in a readable koi silhouette, and the bone/amber/rust/smoke palette is exactly the restrained earth-tone register this gallery wants. However, the chain-mode brief explicitly requires the piece to 'read as the parent [Aizawa attractor] after the word has passed through it (NOT a fresh start),' and this is unmistakably a fresh koi form with zero Aizawa lineage — the double-loop butterfly topology should still be structurally present, perhaps with fluid-advection currents pulling its lobes into a swimming gesture. To fix: initialize home positions from the parent 2n2 Aizawa attractor point cloud, then let the spring targets gradually deform those lobes into a koi-like swimming motion so the ancestry is legible.

v2.feedback: Strong chain execution: Aizawa topology is genuinely preserved via spring-back while point-vortex Biot-Savart advection creates the 'ink in still water' distortion the concept promises. Camera is fixed and contemplative at a reasonable distance. Two refinements: the 600 ambient dust motes risk reading as noise rather than atmosphere — reduce to ~150 or remove entirely so the Aizawa silhouette dominates; and with additive blending on the main particles, verify the color ramp stays in the restrained earth-tone range at accumulation peaks — additive wash-out to near-white would undermine the midnight palette. Consider a subtle fog or depth fade to emphasize the double-loop z-depth and make the spike-and-disk topology even more legible in the first 2 seconds.
